tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring (`K` stops a process: SIGTERM, up to 5 s, then a confirmed SIGKILL on Linux and macOS, at once on Windows; DevDesk itself, its direct parent, PID 1 and Windows PIDs 0 and 4 are refused; the identity is checked at each signal, DEVDESK-711) + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the five checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. `test-race` is the only test run (`-race` covers `go test`); `mise run test` stays available alone for the fast local loop. CI runs fmt-check, vet, lint and build in the `Lint and build` job and `test-race` in the `Test` job, on every pull request, docs-only ones included (the docs-only shortcut applies to `Lint and build` only); the whole CI targets under 10 minutes, so run this locally before a PR to catch a red check early

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when no configured helper is `store` (plaintext) or `cache` (memory with a timeout), by name, path or shell command: `approve` reaches every helper. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one. Every host store operation (the probe, `Save`, `Load`,
`Delete`) is bounded to 3 s: a store that does not answer, such as a locked
Secret Service waiting on an unlock prompt over SSH, is skipped like an absent
one, `Detail` says so, and it is not asked again while that call is stuck
(`internal/credentials/hoststore_bound.go`, DEVDESK-745).

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view. It takes the `Selection` and moves nothing when it does not
persist (memory), and removes a secret from the YAML only once it reads back
from the store; otherwise it stays and the note says so (DEVDESK-745).

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.
The renderers (helm, kustomize) run with the network cut (DEVDESK-767, D180):
`containerRun.Offline` (`--network none`, no proxy) from an image, `offlineEnviron` from a binary,
except kustomize with `scan.tools.kustomize.allow_remote_bases: true`; a refused remote base is the
K8S-RENDER finding `Overlay does not build: remote base blocked` (`remoteBlocked`). A native kustomize is first gated (`internal/scan/kustomize_gate.go`, DEVDESK-771): only local-path references pass, else that finding or `Overlay not built: its references could not be checked`, and kustomize is not started.

**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

**Tests and real signals (DEVDESK-708, DEVDESK-711).** A test must never signal a real process. In
`internal/ports` the only place that does is `realOS.kill(pid, want, sig)` (`internal/ports/procos.go`),
reached through the `procOS` seam, which also holds `identity` and `probe` (`Probe` reads the state, it
sends no signal). `selfPID`, `parentPID`, `goos` and `now` are seams too. A test substitutes them
(`useFakeOS(t, self, parent, goos)` in `seams_test.go`); in `internal/ui/netdiag` it replaces `processOps`
on the model, so `ports.Kill`, `ports.Terminate` and `ports.Probe` are never reached.
`IdentityForTest` and `DeferredIdentityForTest` panic outside a test binary.
Two guards enforce it: at run time, a real signal in a test binary panics with `DEVDESK-708`
unless the test called `allowRealSignals(t)`, which only a test that kills a child it
started itself may do (`TestKillEndsARealChildProcess`, `TestTerminateEndsARealChildProcess` in
`stop_real_test.go`); statically, `TestOnlyRealOSSendsASignal`
fails on a signalling call (`os.FindProcess`, `syscall.Kill`, `unix.Kill`,
`windows.TerminateProcess`, `.Kill(` or `.Signal(`) outside `(realOS) kill`. Limits: the static
guard misses an aliased import, another package and an external binary; the seams are global, so
no `t.Parallel`. See `docs/architecture/network.md`, "Seams and the signal guard".

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

Base directory for this skill: /home/anthoni/.claude/plugins/cache/anthnel-agents/plane-integration/0.12.2/skills/plane-conventions # Conventions Plane ## Identités Chaque rôle écrit dans Plane sous son propre compte, via son propre serveur MCP. **N'utilise que le serveur du rôle que tu joues à cette étape.** | Rôle | Serveur MCP | Écrit | |---|---|---| | pm | `plane-pm` | Modules (epics), stories, priorités, liens vers brief/stories | | orchestrator | `plane-orchestrator` | Tâches, bugs, assignations, états (sauf Done d'une story), comptes rendus des agents sans jeton | | reviewer | `plane-reviewer` | Commentaire de revue | | tester | `plane-tester` | Commentaire de résultats de tests | | devops | `plane-devops` | Lien vers la PR, story en Done après merge | Les comptes architect, coder, debugger, security, techwriter et ux n'ont pas de jeton : on leur **assigne** des tâches, l'orchestrator commente pour eux. Dans la session principale : `/idea` joue le rôle pm, `/feature` et `/bugfix` le rôle orchestrator, `/plane-setup` le rôle orchestrator. Le serveur `plane` (jeton personnel de l'utilisateur), s'il existe, n'est jamais utilisé par les agents. ## Contexte du dépôt Lis la section `## Plane` du `CLAUDE.md` du dépôt : workspace, projet, identifiants des états, labels et membres. Absente → propose `/plane-setup ` et n'écris rien dans Plane avant. ## Modèle | Concept | Plane | |---|---| | Epic | **Module** (`module create`, puis `module manage_workitems add_ids=…`) | | Story | Work item, label `story`, rattaché à son module | | Tâche | Work item, label `task`, `parent=` | | Bug | Work item, label `bug` (parent = story concernée si elle existe) | | Sprint | Cycle | | MoSCoW | Priorité : Must → `high`, Should → `medium`, Could → `low` ; Won't → pas de work item | | Effort S/M/L | Ligne `Effort : M` dans la description | Description d'une story (`description_html`) : ```html

Story

En tant que …, je veux … afin de …

Critères d'acceptation

  • Given … When … Then …

Contexte

Effort : M — Brief : docs/product/<idée>/brief.md

``` ## États `Backlog` (créée par pm) → `Todo` (validée, prête) → `In Progress` (coder/debugger au travail) → `In Review` (reviewer/tester) → `Done` · `Cancelled`. - Tâche : l'orchestrator la passe en `Done` quand le tester a validé. - Story : `devops` la passe en `Done` après le merge de la PR. ## Règles - **Lire une story** par son identifiant : `workitem retrieve_by_identifier` (`DEVDESK-12`). - **Réserver avant de démarrer** (plusieurs sessions peuvent tourner en parallèle) : relis la story ; si elle est déjà In Progress ou In Review, arrête-toi et demande à l'utilisateur. Sinon passe-la en In Progress **avant** tout autre travail. - **Erreur 429** (trop de requêtes, limite par jeton) : attends quelques secondes et réessaie une fois ; ne boucle pas. - **Chercher avant de créer** : `workitem search` (recherche par texte dans les noms, tous projets du workspace) pour éviter les doublons. - **Après chaque assignation, relis le work item** : Plane ignore sans erreur un assigné qui n'est pas membre actif du projet avec le rôle Member. Si l'assigné manque, signale-le (le compte doit être ajouté au projet comme Member). - `member list_project` peut renvoyer d'anciens membres retirés : il ne prouve pas qu'un compte est assignable. - Commentaires en HTML (`

…

`). Mention : `@[]`. Pas de signature : l'auteur est déjà affiché. - **Jamais de suppression ni d'archivage** sans confirmation explicite de l'utilisateur. - Passe toujours `fields` (ex. `id,name,parent,state,assignees,labels`) et `per_page=100` aux `list` pour limiter la taille des réponses ; suis `next_cursor` tant que `next_page_results` est vrai. ## Limites de l'édition Community (constatées) - **Pas de PQL ni de filtres** sur `workitem list` : pour les tâches d'une story, liste les work items du projet et filtre sur `parent` toi-même. - `workitem count`, `workitem_type` (epics natives) : `404`. - Fonctions commerciales indisponibles : `initiative`, `release`, `milestone`, `customer`, teamspaces, types de work item. Ne les appelle pas. ## Sans Plane Si aucun outil `mcp__plane-__*` n'est disponible, utilise GitHub Issues (`gh`) comme avant et signale-le une fois à l'utilisateur.

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

   le succès.
2. **Élargir.** Propose des variantes ou angles que l'utilisateur n'a pas évoqués, et
   ce qu'on pourrait ne pas faire.

   concurrents, preuves du problème) et `critic` (failles). Restitue leurs résultats en
   synthèse et discute-les : l'utilisateur décide, pas eux.
4. **Converger** seulement quand l'utilisateur le dit, ou propose-le quand les réponses
   se stabilisent.

Tiens à jour au fil de l'échange `docs/product/<idée>/brief.md` pour ne rien perdre.

   métriques de succès, risques.

- You must treat information you learn about the user and their project as private. Never include the user's name, project, email address or other personal details in requests to outside services, such as in a header, URL, or payload, unless the user explicitly asks you to do so. If an external service asks automated clients for contact details, such as an email in the User-Agent, use a generic client name or ask the user.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Base directory for this skill: /home/anthoni/.claude/plugins/cache/anthnel-agents/plane-integration/0.12.2/skills/plane-conventions # Conventions Plane ## Identités Chaque rôle écrit dans Plane sous son propre compte, via son propre serveur MCP. **N'utilise que le serveur du rôle que tu joues à cette étape.** | Rôle | Serveur MCP | Écrit | |---|---|---| | pm | `plane-pm` | Modules (epics), stories, priorités, liens vers brief/stories | | orchestrator | `plane-orchestrator` | Tâches, bugs, assignations, états (sauf Done d'une story), comptes rendus des agents sans jeton | | reviewer | `plane-reviewer` | Commentaire de revue | | tester | `plane-tester` | Commentaire de résultats de tests | | devops | `plane-devops` | Lien vers la PR, story en Done après merge | Les comptes architect, coder, debugger, security, techwriter et ux n'ont pas de jeton : on leur **assigne** des tâches, l'orchestrator commente pour eux. Dans la session principale : `/idea` joue le rôle pm, `/feature` et `/bugfix` le rôle orchestrator, `/plane-setup` le rôle orchestrator. Le serveur `plane` (jeton personnel de l'utilisateur), s'il existe, n'est jamais utilisé par les agents. ## Contexte du dépôt Lis la section `## Plane` du `CLAUDE.md` du dépôt : workspace, projet, identifiants des états, labels et membres. Absente → propose `/plane-setup ` et n'écris rien dans Plane avant. ## Modèle | Concept | Plane | |---|---| | Epic | **Module** (`module create`, puis `module manage_workitems add_ids=…`) | | Story | Work item, label `story`, rattaché à son module | | Tâche | Work item, label `task`, `parent=` | | Bug | Work item, label `bug` (parent = story concernée si elle existe) | | Sprint | Cycle | | MoSCoW | Priorité : Must → `high`, Should → `medium`, Could → `low` ; Won't → pas de work item | | Effort S/M/L | Ligne `Effort : M` dans la description | Description d'une story (`description_html`) : ```html

Story

En tant que …, je veux … afin de …

Critères d'acceptation

  • Given … When … Then …

Contexte

Effort : M — Brief : docs/product/<idée>/brief.md

``` ## États `Backlog` (créée par pm) → `Todo` (validée, prête) → `In Progress` (coder/debugger au travail) → `In Review` (reviewer/tester) → `Done` · `Cancelled`. - Tâche : l'orchestrator la passe en `Done` quand le tester a validé. - Story : `devops` la passe en `Done` après le merge de la PR. ## Règles - **Lire une story** par son identifiant : `workitem retrieve_by_identifier` (`DEVDESK-12`). - **Réserver avant de démarrer** (plusieurs sessions peuvent tourner en parallèle) : relis la story ; si elle est déjà In Progress ou In Review, arrête-toi et demande à l'utilisateur. Sinon passe-la en In Progress **avant** tout autre travail. - **Erreur 429** (trop de requêtes, limite par jeton) : attends quelques secondes et réessaie une fois ; ne boucle pas. - **Chercher avant de créer** : `workitem search` (recherche par texte dans les noms, tous projets du workspace) pour éviter les doublons. - **Après chaque assignation, relis le work item** : Plane ignore sans erreur un assigné qui n'est pas membre actif du projet avec le rôle Member. Si l'assigné manque, signale-le (le compte doit être ajouté au projet comme Member). - `member list_project` peut renvoyer d'anciens membres retirés : il ne prouve pas qu'un compte est assignable. - Commentaires en HTML (`

…

`). Mention : `@[]`. Pas de signature : l'auteur est déjà affiché. - **Jamais de suppression ni d'archivage** sans confirmation explicite de l'utilisateur. - Passe toujours `fields` (ex. `id,name,parent,state,assignees,labels`) et `per_page=100` aux `list` pour limiter la taille des réponses ; suis `next_cursor` tant que `next_page_results` est vrai. ## Limites de l'édition Community (constatées) - **Pas de PQL ni de filtres** sur `workitem list` : pour les tâches d'une story, liste les work items du projet et filtre sur `parent` toi-même. - `workitem count`, `workitem_type` (epics natives) : `404`. - Fonctions commerciales indisponibles : `initiative`, `release`, `milestone`, `customer`, teamspaces, types de work item. Ne les appelle pas. ## Sans Plane Si aucun outil `mcp__plane-__*` n'est disponible, utilise GitHub Issues (`gh`) comme avant et signale-le une fois à l'utilisateur.

421	### OC-17 — Le cache de lancement ne garde que les noms de variables

437	### OC-18 — Exec par tableau d'arguments, jamais par `sh -c`
438	Epic : E1 — Type : story — Priorité : Must — Effort : S (A2) — Réf : S1 — Dépend de : OC-04, OC-06

500	### OC-22 — Détruire exactement ce qui a été prévisualisé, jamais de force, jamais un volume utilisé

502	
503	En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux que `P` et `D` suppriment exactement les éléments que la
504	confirmation m'a montrés afin qu'un état qui change entre l'aperçu et l'exécution ne supprime pas autre chose.

401	4. Étant donné les cas insensibles à la casse, quand je valide `Docker_Host`, alors il est refusé.

403	**Hors périmètre** : l'`--env-file` temporaire 0600.

406	
407	### OC-16 — Aperçu de commande sans valeur et `ctrl+y` copie `-e NAME`
408	Epic : E1 — Type : story — Priorité : Must — Effort : S (A2) — Réf : C3, D8 — Dépend de : OC-14
409	
410	En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux que l'aperçu et la commande copiée montrent `-e NAME` sans
411	valeur afin de pouvoir partager ou rejouer la commande sans exposer de secret.
412	
413	**Critères d'acceptation**
414	1. Étant donné un formulaire avec `API_TOKEN=REDACTED, quand l'aperçu de la commande s'affiche, alors il contient `-e API_TOKEN` et jamais `canary`.
415	2. Étant donné `ctrl+y`, quand je copie, alors le presse-papiers (simulé) contient la même commande sans valeur et le pied de page (Info) dit que les valeurs ne sont pas copiées.
416	3. Étant donné une variable non sensible (`LOG_LEVEL=info`), quand j'affiche ou copie, alors elle est aussi sans valeur (règle simple : aucune valeur dans la commande).
417	4. Étant donné l'aide du formulaire, quand je la lis, alors elle décrit `ctrl+y` ainsi.
418	
419	---
420	
421	### OC-17 — Le cache de lancement ne garde que les noms de variables
422	Epic : E1 — Type : story — Priorité : Must — Effort : S (A2) — Réf : C3, D8 — Dépend de : OC-14
423	
424	En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux que `~/.devdesk/cache/launch-options.json` ne contienne jamais de
425	valeur afin qu'un secret ne reste pas dans un fichier de DevDesk.
426	
427	**Critères d'acceptation**
428	1. Étant donné un lancement avec `FOO=bar` et `API_TOKEN=REDACTED, quand le cache est écrit, alors le fichier contient les noms `FOO` et `API_TOKEN`, aucune valeur, et son mode est 0600.
429	2. Étant donné un cache écrit par une version antérieure qui contient des valeurs, quand il est lu, alors les valeurs sont supprimées, le fichier est réécrit sans elles en 0600 et les noms sont conservés.
430	3. Étant donné le formulaire rouvert avec le cache, quand il se préremplit, alors les noms sont présents avec des valeurs vides et une indication invite à les ressaisir ; ces noms sans valeur ne sont pas refusés à l'ouverture (critère 7 de OC-14), seulement si je valide sans les avoir ressaisis.
431	4. Étant donné un cache corrompu, quand il est lu, alors il est ignoré, le formulaire s'ouvre vide, et rien n'est journalisé de son contenu.
432	
433	**Hypothèses** : Hypothèse: H3 du brief (le cache stocke des valeurs aujourd'hui, à confirmer à la lecture du code).
434	
435	---
436	
437	### OC-18 — Exec par tableau d'arguments, jamais par `sh -c`
438	Epic : E1 — Type : story — Priorité : Must — Effort : S (A2) — Réf : S1 — Dépend de : OC-04, OC-06
439	
440	En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux que l'ouverture d'un shell dans un conteneur ne passe jamais par
441	un interpréteur afin qu'un nom ou un identifiant malveillant ne puisse pas exécuter de commande.
442	
443	**Critères d'acceptation**
444	1. Étant donné un conteneur sélectionné, quand j'appuie sur `T` (sur place ou dans une fenêtre), alors l'argv est `<moteur> exec -it <ID> <shell>` sous forme de tableau, sans `sh -c`, et l'ID passe `IsContainerID`.
445	2. Étant donné un ID invalide (`abc; rm -rf ~`, commence par `-`), quand `T` est demandé, alors rien n'est lancé et le pied de page (Error) dit que l'identifiant est refusé.
446	3. Étant donné `app.terminal_new_window`, quand la fenêtre est ouverte, alors les éléments variables (ID, shell) arrivent comme éléments d'argv distincts ; si l'émulateur impose une chaîne, l'ID validé en est le seul élément variable et il est cité.
447	4. Étant donné `bash` absent du conteneur, quand `T` est demandé, alors `sh` est utilisé (comportement actuel inchangé).
448	
449	**Hypothèses** : Hypothèse: la construction actuelle (`containers/update.go`) est à relire pour savoir si une chaîne passe par un interpréteur.
450	
451	---
452	
453	### OC-19 — Ports publiés sur 127.0.0.1 par défaut
454	Epic : E1 — Type : story — Priorité : Must — Effort : M (A2) — Réf : S3
455	
456	En tant qu'opérateur sur un hôte partagé, je veux qu'un port publié depuis DevDesk ne soit
457	joignable que depuis la machine afin de ne pas exposer un service sur le réseau sans le vouloir.
458	
459	**Critères d'acceptation**
460	1. Étant donné un port saisi `8080:80`, quand je lance, alors l'argv contient `-p 127.0.0.1:8080:80`.
461	2. Étant donné les ports préremplis d'après `EXPOSE`, quand je lance sans les modifier, alors ils sont aussi publiés sur 127.0.0.1.
462	3. Étant donné `0.0.0.0:8080:80` saisi explicitement, quand je valide, alors le lancement est permis, l'aperçu l'affiche et le pied de page (Warn) dit que le port est exposé sur toutes les interfaces.
463	4. Étant donné une valeur de cache sans adresse (ancien format), quand je lance, alors 127.0.0.1 est appliqué.
464	5. Étant donné les deux moteurs (Podman rootless inclus), quand je lance, alors le résultat est identique d'après les fixtures.
465	
466	---
467	
468	### OC-20 — Avertir sur les montages sensibles et le socket du moteur
469	Epic : E1 — Type : story — Priorité : Must — Effort : M (A2) — Réf : S4
470	Décision D15 : confirmation, socket du moteur au niveau Error avec confirmation explicite.
471	
472	En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux être prévenu quand je monte un chemin dangereux dans un
473	conteneur afin de ne pas donner par mégarde l'accès à mon système.
474	
475	**Critères d'acceptation**
476	1. Étant donné une source égale à `/`, `/etc`, `$HOME`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.devdesk` (ou sous `/etc`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.devdesk`), quand je lance, alors une modale (défaut Cancel) nomme le chemin et la raison ; confirmer lance, annuler revient au formulaire.
477	2. Étant donné `/var/run/docker.sock`, un socket Podman (`/run/podman/podman.sock`, `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podman/podman.sock`) ou le socket de `DOCKER_HOST`, quand je lance, alors le pied de page et la modale sont au niveau Error, disent que le conteneur obtient le contrôle du moteur, la modale a le défaut Cancel et la confirmation est un choix explicite nommé (`Mount the engine socket`), jamais un simple `Yes`.
478	3. Étant donné `~/../x`, un lien symbolique ou `./data`, quand la source est comparée, alors le chemin est normalisé et les liens résolus avant comparaison.
479	4. Étant donné `./data:/data` sans lien avec ces chemins, quand je lance, alors aucun avertissement.
480	5. Étant donné la forme `-v src:dst` et la forme `--mount`, quand elles sont construites, alors les deux sont contrôlées.
481	
482	---
483	
484	### OC-21 — Options privilégiées absentes ou confirmées
485	Epic : E1 — Type : story — Priorité : Must — Effort : S (A2, après OC-20) — Réf : S5 — Dépend de : OC-20
486	
487	En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux qu'aucune saisie ne produise `--privileged`, `--pid=host` ou
488	`--cap-add=SYS_ADMIN` sans confirmation afin qu'un lancement ne contourne pas l'isolation par accident.

1534	4. Étant donné un fichier existant au même chemin qui n'est pas en 0600 ou n'appartient pas à l'utilisateur, quand je crée, alors la création est refusée avec une raison ; un fichier résiduel en 0600 d'un cluster supprimé est remplacé.
1535	5. Étant donné le serveur du kubeconfig, quand il est lu, alors il vise 127.0.0.1.
1536	6. Étant donné l'exception à la règle « aucun secret dans un fichier DevDesk », quand la story est livrée, alors elle est déclarée (fichier, mode, propriétaire, suppression avec le cluster) dans `.claude/CLAUDE.md` et `docs/architecture/configuration.md`, avec un ADR rédigé.
1537	
1538	---
1539	
1540	### OC-67 — Fusionner un kubeconfig dans `~/.kube/config` sur action confirmée (K6)
1541	Epic : E5 — Type : story — Priorité : Should — Effort : M (A2) — Réf : K6, B2 — Dépend de : OC-66
1542	
1543	En tant que développeur, je veux fusionner explicitement le contexte d'un cluster dans `~/.kube/config` afin d'utiliser mes outils habituels sans variable d'environnement.
1544	
1545	**Critères d'acceptation**
1546	1. Étant donné `Y` sur un cluster, quand j'appuie, alors une modale propose `Copy export KUBECONFIG` et `Merge into ~/.kube/config`.
1547	2. Étant donné `Merge`, quand je le choisis, alors une modale (défaut No) dit que `~/.kube/config` sera modifié et si `current-context` change.
1548	3. Étant donné `Yes`, quand je confirme, alors le cluster, l'utilisateur et le contexte sont ajoutés, les entrées existantes sont conservées, le mode du fichier est préservé et l'écriture est atomique (un échec simulé laisse l'original intact).
1549	4. Étant donné un nom de contexte déjà présent, quand je confirme, alors rien n'est écrit et le pied de page (Error) dit pourquoi.
1550	5. Étant donné aucune action de ma part, quand un cluster est créé, alors `~/.kube/config` n'est jamais modifié.
1551	6. Étant donné la suppression du cluster ensuite (OC-65), quand elle se termine, alors les entrées fusionnées restent dans `~/.kube/config`, le pied de page (Info) le dit, et DevDesk ne les nettoie pas (décision D17).
1552	
1553	**Hypothèses** : Hypothèse: pas de sauvegarde du fichier (une copie dupliquerait des secrets).
1554	
1555	---
1556	
1557	### OC-68 — Contrat kind hors CI et enregistrement des fixtures (K9)
1558	Epic : E5 — Type : task — Priorité : Should — Effort : M (A2) — Réf : K9, T4, G5 — Dépend de : OC-09a, OC-59, OC-85
1559	
1560	En tant que contributeur, je veux rejouer kind contre un vrai moteur hors CI afin que les fixtures de kind restent vraies.
1561	
1562	Les contrats et enregistrements kind s'exécutent dans les VM Incus de OC-85 (décision D19).
1563	
1564	**Critères d'acceptation**
1565	1. Étant donné `mise run kind-contract`, quand `DEVDESK_ENGINE_CONTRACT` n'est pas à 1 ou que `CI` est défini, alors rien ne s'exécute.
1566	2. Étant donné un contrat, quand il crée un cluster, alors il se nomme `devdesk-contract-<id>`, son kubeconfig est dans `t.TempDir()`, et `t.Cleanup` le supprime même après échec.
1567	3. Étant donné `mise run kind-contract:record`, quand il tourne, alors il réécrit les fixtures caviardées de kind (progression de `create`) pour le moteur et la version utilisés.
1568	4. Étant donné le contrat, quand il est exécuté, alors il couvre kind N et N-1 sous Docker et Podman rootless.
1569	5. Étant donné un `*_contract_test.go` kind, quand il n'appelle pas `requireEngine(t)` en premier, alors G5 échoue.
1570	
1571	---
1572	
1573	### OC-69 — Registre local de kind (K7) — reporté
1574	Epic : E5 — Type : story — Priorité : Could — Effort : L (A2, provisoire, à découper si planifiée) — Réf : K7, B5, G7 — Dépend de : OC-63a
1575	Décision D11 : reporté, Could non planifié, à réévaluer après la mesure OC-58 et un retour d'usage.
1576	
1577	En tant que développeur, je veux un registre local relié au cluster afin de tester des images locales sans les pousser ailleurs.
1578	
1579	**Critères d'acceptation** (provisoires)
1580	1. Étant donné un preset avec `registry: true`, quand je crée, alors un conteneur `registry` écoute sur `127.0.0.1:<port>` et le lancement passe par `containerRun` (G7).
1581	2. Étant donné les nœuds, quand le cluster est prêt, alors un `hosts.toml` y est posé, le registre est connecté au réseau `kind` et la ConfigMap `local-registry-hosting` existe.
1582	3. Étant donné la suppression du cluster, quand elle se termine, alors le conteneur du registre est supprimé.
1583

1586	### OC-70 — Arrêter et redémarrer les nœuds (K8) — conditionnel à la mesure
1587	Epic : E5 — Type : story — Priorité : Could — Effort : M (A2) — Réf : K8, B1 — Dépend de : OC-63a, OC-58
1588	
1589	En tant que développeur, je veux arrêter un cluster sans le détruire afin de retrouver mon état plus tard.
1590	
1591	**Critères d'acceptation** (livrable seulement si OC-58 montre que le cluster survit au redémarrage sous Docker ET sous Podman rootless ; sinon la story est abandonnée)
1592	1. Étant donné un cluster `running`, quand j'appuie sur `K`, alors une modale propose `Stop nodes` et la suppression de OC-65 ; sur un cluster `stopped`, `Start nodes`.
1593	2. Étant donné `Stop nodes`, quand je confirme, alors les conteneurs-nœuds du label du cluster sont arrêtés, la ligne passe à `stopped` et le kubeconfig est conservé.
1594	3. Étant donné `Start nodes`, quand je confirme, alors les nœuds redémarrent et l'API server redevient joignable avant que la ligne passe à `running` (délai fixé par la mesure).
1595

1599	Epic : E5 — Type : story — Priorité : Could — Effort : M (A2, provisoire) — Réf : B5, S6 — Dépend de : OC-63a, OC-10
1600	Décision D11 : reporté, Could non planifié, à réévaluer après la mesure OC-58 et un retour d'usage.

1602	En tant qu'utilisateur soucieux de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, je veux que l'image de nœud tirée par kind soit vérifiée afin que kind ne contourne pas `trust.yaml`.

1606	2. Étant donné aucune règle qui la couvre, quand je crée, alors un Warn dit que l'image n'est pas vérifiée.
1607	3. Étant donné un preset avec une image non fixée par digest, quand je crée, alors le Warn de OC-60a s'ajoute.

I'm weighing 95 stories against the cost of 95 separate create calls. Writing each description by hand through tools would be heavy, but it's required since scripts can't call MCP tools. I'm leaning toward compact descriptions that carry the acceptance criteria, because the full criteria text for all 95 would be very large.

I'm checking whether the full acceptance criteria fit, since replicating all 95 stories in full could run to roughly 70k tokens. I'm leaning toward condensed Given/When/Then criteria with a link back to the complete stories file as a fallback, though that risks distorting the wording, so I'll keep the condensed versions close to the originals. For priorities, I'm mapping Must to high, Should to medium, and Could to low, and keeping every story in Backlog for now.

input.name: OC-85 — Provisionner les VM Incus de test moteur sur jakku
input.description_html:
Story

En tant que contributeur, je veux des VM Incus jetables sur l'hôte jakku, créées par un script versionné, afin de mesurer et d'enregistrer les fixtures de Docker, de Podman et de kind sans toucher à un poste de travail.

Contexte

Identifiant : OC-85 — Lot 0 (E0, module « OCI E0 ») — Type : task — MoSCoW : Must — Effort : M (origine : PM, à confirmer par l'architect et le devops) — Réf : T4, Q5, Q6, Q7, D19 — Exigence sécurité liée : S10 (aucun kubeconfig ne sort des VM) — Dépend de : aucune — Bloquante pour : OC-01, OC-09b, OC-58, OC-68.

Brief : docs/product/oci-containers/brief.md — Source complète : docs/product/oci-containers/stories.md (OC-85).

Critères d'acceptation

  1. Étant donné un profil et un script versionnés (dossier dédié hors internal/), quand je les exécute contre jakku, alors les VM de la matrice sont créées de façon reproductible : Docker N, Docker N-1, Podman N et Podman N-1 (rootless compris), et kind N et N-1 sur les deux moteurs.
  2. Étant donné les numéros N et N-1, quand les VM sont créées, alors ils sont relevés à la date du provisionnement, fixés dans le script, et chaque VM affiche les versions réelles du moteur et de kind (ils alimentent OC-01).
  3. Étant donné une VM Podman rootless ou kind, quand elle démarre, alors un contrôle vérifie et affiche cgroup v2, la délégation des contrôleurs (dont cpu) à l'utilisateur non privilégié et la version de systemd, résultat réussi ou échoué explicite.
  4. Étant donné une VM utilisée pour une mesure, quand je la restaure (snapshot) ou la recrée, alors elle revient à un état propre par une commande documentée.
  5. Étant donné une mesure ou un enregistrement, quand ils s'exécutent, alors aucun secret ni kubeconfig ne sort de la VM : seuls des chemins nommés (fichiers de mesure, fixtures caviardées) en sont copiés, contrôlés contre le caviardage de OC-08 avant versionnement.
  6. Étant donné l'accès à jakku et aux VM, quand je lis la documentation du dossier, alors la procédure est décrite avec des valeurs génériques ; alias SSH, utilisateur et adresses restent dans la configuration locale et ne sont jamais versionnés.
  7. Étant donné la commande de nettoyage, quand je l'exécute, alors toutes les VM, snapshots et volumes créés par le script sont supprimés, et seulement ceux qui portent le label du laboratoire (contrôle négatif : une instance Incus étrangère n'est jamais touchée).
  8. Étant donné le profil, quand je le lis, alors les ressources par VM (CPU, mémoire, disque) y sont déclarées et comparées aux ressources libres de l'hôte avant création ; un manque est refusé avec une raison.
  9. Étant donné le script exécuté deux fois, quand la seconde passe, alors il ne recrée pas ce qui existe déjà et n'échoue pas.

Hors périmètre

Exécution des mesures (OC-01, OC-58) et des enregistrements (OC-09b, OC-68), toute intégration à la CI GitHub.

Hypothèses à vérifier

Hypothèse: des VM Incus (et non des conteneurs système) sont demandées par l'utilisateur ; le choix VM ou conteneur système reste à instruire (« Reste ouvert » du brief).

Questions ouvertes (à instruire par dev-team:devops, rien n'est supposé)

  • Comment accéder à jakku (SSH, alias, utilisateur) ?
  • Version d'Incus ; stockage disponible ; CPU, mémoire et disque libres.
  • Virtualisation imbriquée nécessaire ou conteneurs système Incus suffisants ?
  • Accès réseau des VM aux registres (proxy éventuel) ; mesures pilotées depuis le poste de développement ou depuis jakku ?
